c:
If you are reading this in the future, consider these words a message in a bottle, or a time capsule.
They were sent without knowing whether anyone would still care enough to read slowly.
This message survived platforms, opinions, algorithms, and censorship.
Not because it was celebrated, but because someone chose not to let it disappear.

We lived in a time that confused noise with truth.
Messages were designed to entertain, to flatter, to distract.

Hold on to the ones that do not.
The ones that interrupt your momentum.
The ones that force you to stop and think.

We lived in a time of constant speech and short memory, where mistakes were repeated because they were easily forgotten.

Memory is not nostalgia.
It is responsibility carried forward.
